newsitem.title: INDIA: No nationwide tour for Gandhi's ashes.
newsitem.headline: No nationwide tour for Gandhi's ashes.

text.p: An Indian court has blocked a plan by Mahatma Gandhi's great grandson to take his purported ashes on a nationwide tour before immersing them in the Ganges River, news agencies said on Monday.

The high court of the eastern state of Orissa said on Sunday that the wooden box which Tushar Arun Gandhi says contains his relative's ashes would have to be taken directly to the Ganges and not on a tour, the local agencies said.
After a fast and much media attention, Tushar Arun Gandhi won control in November of the sealed box, which had lain in a vault in the State Bank of India in Cuttack town since 1950.
Gandhi was shot dead by a Hindu fanatic on January 30, 1948, five months after India, spurred by the apostle of non-violence, won independence from Britain. He was cremated in Delhi.
The box, measuring 18 inches by 18 inches by 20 inches (45 cm by 45 cm by 50 cm), bears the inscription "It contains the ashes of Mahatma Gandhi".
But the state's chief minister has called the claims that the box contains Gandhi's ashes "a big hoax".
Gandhi's great grandson had planned to take the ashes across the country on a pilgrimage before immersing them in the Ganges on January 30, the 49th anniversary of the assassination of the Mahatma.
The itinerary would have taken the ashes to sites linked to Gandhi's non-violent campaign against British rule.
But the Orissa chief justice told Tushar Arun Gandhi on Sunday that the ashes would have to be taken straight to the northern city of Allahabad, the Press Trust of India said.

There, in a Hindu ceremony which Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was expected to attend, the ashes were to be immersed at the holy confluence of the Ganges with the Jamuna River and their mythical tributary, the Saraswati River.
